title: Med Spa Gift Card Promotion: Offers, Terms and Accounting (November 2026)
summary: Plan a med spa gift card promotion with bonus-card terms, expiry rules and deferred revenue sorted out, so holiday sales do not become a Q1 problem.
body_markdown:
## Which Gift Card Offers Work for a Med Spa


The bonus card is the offer med spas run most, and the other formats are variations on it. A buyer pays for a card, receives something extra, and the extra only pays out when someone returns to treat.


Published guidance agrees on the shape. Mindbody lists[holiday gift card ideas for med spas](https://www.mindbodyonline.com/business/education/blog/6-holiday-marketing-strategies-your-med-spa) that include rewarding the buyer with an extra, and Zenoti's guide to[turning gift card sales into repeat clients](https://www.zenoti.com/en-uk/thecheckin/medspa-gift-card-sales-marketing) treats the gift card as an acquisition channel, since recipients are often people who have never booked with you.


Offer What the buyer gets Main risk Best for


Bonus card Buy $100, receive a $20 to $25 card Bonus used on low-margin services Most clinics, November to December


Tiered bonus Larger bonus at $200 and $500 Complexity at the counter Clinics with high-ticket packages


Service-specific card A named treatment, such as a facial Price changes after the card is sold Clinics with fixed-price services


Discounted card $80 for a $100 card Teaches patients to wait for a sale Slow months only


Free add-on at redemption Extra service when the card is used Giving away treatment time Clinics with open chair time


The gap in most of these guides is what happens after the sale. Zenoti reports that first-time visitors make up 24% of gift card redemptions in its 2025 benchmark data, which is the reason to design the redemption visit, not only the purchase.


## How to Structure a Bonus Gift Card So It Pays Off


A bonus card pays off when it costs you service margin and not cash. A $25 bonus redeemed on a service with a 60% gross margin costs about $10 in direct cost, while the same $25 on a per-unit injectable can cost most of what you charge. That figure is an illustration, so use your own margins.


Four decisions keep the offer profitable:


- **Separate the two cards.** The base card is the patient's money and stays usable. The bonus card is yours and can carry limits.
- **Put an end date on the bonus only.** January through March is a common window because it fills the quiet weeks after the holidays.
- **Choose what the bonus covers.** Services with healthy margin qualify. Per-unit injectables, retail already on sale and membership dues do not.
- **Cap the offer.** A per-patient limit and a closing date stop a reseller buying fifty cards the night before the promotion ends.


If you already run stackable offers, apply the same rule from a[med spa discount policy](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-discount-policy) : one reduction per ticket unless the table says otherwise. A bonus card used on top of a member rate and a seasonal special is three discounts nobody priced together.


## Gift Card Terms to Write Before You Launch


Write the terms on one screen before the first card is sold, because the front desk will quote them out loud for the whole season. A short version covers five lines: what the card is worth, what it covers, whether it expires, whether it can be transferred, and what the bonus excludes.


A patient who asks "does this expire?" should get one sentence back. Clinics that answer differently at different desks create the dispute later, usually in a conversation with a patient who was told something different a year earlier. One practice we spoke with this fall found exactly that: a patient holding a card from an earlier promotion had been told verbally that gift cards never expire, and the clinic chose to honor it.


Pair the terms with your[package refund policy](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-package-refund-policy) so a refund request on a gift card gets the same answer as one on a prepaid package. Decide as well whether a card can be refunded to the purchaser, and whether you will replace a lost one.


## Gift Card Expiration Rules Every Med Spa Should Know


Federal rules set a five-year floor on store gift cards. Under[12 CFR 1005.20](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/12/1005.20) , a card may carry an expiration date only if the underlying funds last at least five years from the date it was issued, and the card must show the expiration date or say the funds do not expire.


The same section excludes loyalty, award and promotional cards from those definitions, which is why a free bonus card can carry a short window. The exclusion has conditions. A promotional card must state that it is issued for promotional purposes and show the expiration date for the underlying funds on the front of the card. Dormancy and inactivity fees are limited too: none unless the card has sat unused for a year, with the fee stated on the card and no more than one a month.


Treat this as the minimum. Some states are stricter than the federal rule and a few restrict expiry on paid cards altogether, so confirm the rule where you operate before printing terms, and have counsel read the final version. This is general information, not legal advice.


## How to Account for Gift Card Sales


A gift card sale is a liability, not revenue, until the card is redeemed. When a patient buys a card in December, you record the cash and an equal deferred revenue balance, then recognize revenue as services are delivered. Our guide to[seasonal cash flow for med spas](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-seasonal-cash-flow-planning) walks through why a December that looks strong can hand its work to January.


Take a clinic that sells $60,000 in cards between Thanksgiving and New Year's. Most of that is redeemed in the first quarter, when payroll and rent are due, and the cash was already spent on holiday inventory and marketing. Track three numbers weekly during the promotion: cards sold, cards redeemed and outstanding balance. The outstanding balance is the one that belongs on your[KPI dashboard](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-kpi-tracking) .


Ask your accountant how to book the bonus value. Many clinics treat it as a marketing cost recognized at redemption, but that is a decision for your books and not something to copy from a blog.


## Common Gift Card Problems Behind the Front Desk


Most gift card trouble comes from three places: the wrong recipient contact, a balance that did not follow a migration, and a card that was voided or expired in the old system. All three arrive as a patient standing at checkout with a card in her hand.


**The wrong recipient number.** A buyer purchases a $150 card online for a friend and types the friend's phone number with one digit off. The text is delivered, to a stranger. The recipient never sees it, the buyer calls the clinic, and the front desk has to work out whether the card was lost or just sent to the wrong person. Confirm the recipient's name and number when you sell the card in person, and read the number back.


**The card nobody can find.** A patient presents a $250 card from the previous software, but it is missing. The old system had voided it, so it was left out of the export. The patient was told the card never expires, so the clinic honored it by recreating it. In the same clean-up, the clinic found close to a thousand older cards, worth six figures in total, that still showed a balance in the old system. That is why a migration plan needs a rule for expired and voided cards.


**The bonus used the wrong way.** Without a named promotion and clear exclusions, a bonus card lands on a neurotoxin sale because the patient asked and nobody wanted to argue. Our guidance on[patient wallets, credits and split payments](https://decodahealth.com/blog/setting-up-vip-memberships-beauty-banks-and-patient-wallets) covers how a card, a membership credit and a card payment can sit on one ticket without confusion.


## What to Do With Gift Cards When You Switch Software


Gift card balances are one of the places migrations quietly lose money, so export them before cutover and reconcile them after. Ask your old vendor for every card with its issue date, original value, remaining balance and status, including voided and expired cards.


Then make three decisions. First, which cards come across active. Second, which expired cards come across as inactive records, so staff can see the balance and choose to honor one. Third, who is allowed to approve that choice. Our walkthrough of[what transfers in an EMR migration](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-emr-migration-what-transfers) lists the other balances that belong on the same checklist: packages, memberships and credits.


## Using Gift Cards to Bring Recipients Back


A gift card sale is the start of a relationship with the recipient, who may be new to your clinic. Send a short welcome text when the card is activated, offer an easy booking link, and tag the recipient so a redemption visit can be followed by a rebooking message.


Plan the follow-up before the holidays. Sales in November and December tend to be redeemed between January and March, which is when a re-engagement campaign matters most, as covered in our guide to[cohort targeting and re-engagement](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-cohort-targeting-re-engagement) . Check consent before you send, using the rules in[med spa text message consent](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-text-message-consent) .


A related lever is the gift your own members give. Referral credit and gift cards overlap, and a[med spa referral program](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-referral-program) works better when the reward is credit toward your own services and not a cash-like card.


## How Decoda Health Handles Gift Cards


Decoda Health keeps gift card balances in the same checkout as memberships, packages and patient credit, so a ticket can split payment between a card, account credit and a payment card. When a clinic moves over, gift cards are among the balances carried across with patient records and financials, as described on the[memberships page](https://decodahealth.com/products/memberships) .


Practices that sell packages alongside cards can see how prepaid balances sit together on the[packages page](https://decodahealth.com/products/packages) . Whatever software you use, confirm that it can report outstanding gift card balances, because that single number tells you how much of the holiday season you have already spent.


## Final Thoughts on Your Med Spa Gift Card Promotion


Run one offer, write the terms on a single screen, keep the base card free of expiry and put the end date on the bonus. Book every sale as a liability, watch the outstanding balance weekly, and count your old cards before any software change. ## Frequently Asked Questions


What is a good gift card promotion for a med spa?


The most common structure is a bonus card: buy a $100 card and receive a $20 to $25 card to use later. It rewards the buyer, brings the bonus holder back in January, and costs you only the margin on the services redeemed. Keep the terms short, put an end date on the bonus value, and sell the base card as a regular gift card with no expiry.


Can a med spa put an expiration date on a gift card?


Federal rules allow an expiration date on a store gift card only if the funds last at least five years from issue. Promotional cards, such as a bonus card given free with a purchase, are excluded from that rule but must say they are promotional and show the expiry date on the front. Several states are stricter, so check yours before printing terms.


How do you account for gift card sales at a med spa?


A gift card sale is not revenue on the day it is sold. You record the cash and an equal deferred revenue liability, then recognize revenue as the card is redeemed. A clinic that sells $60,000 of cards in December has not earned $60,000. Ask your accountant how to book the bonus value and any unredeemed balances.


Should a bonus gift card be usable on injectables?


Most clinics limit bonus value to services with healthy margin and exclude per-unit injectables, because a 20% bonus on a neurotoxin sale can erase most of the profit. State the exclusion on the card terms and at checkout. Make the exclusions short enough that a buyer can read them in one breath.


What happens to gift cards when a med spa switches software?


Balances have to move with the patient records or you will be honoring them by hand. Export every card with its remaining balance, issue date and expiry status, including cards your old system marked expired or voided. Staff will meet patients holding cards that never came across, so decide up front who can approve restoring one.
